recipes.title: Wasabi Cream Cheese
recipes.source_note: Cream cheese with Japanese wasabi for sinus-clearing heat.
recipes.description: Rich cream cheese with wasabi's distinctive nasal heat. Unique pungency that clears the sinuses - perfect on bagels with smoked salmon.

instructions.text: Heat cream and milk to 75°F (24°C). Add starter, ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet, stir gently. Let set at room temp 12-24 hours.
Ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined strainer. Drain 12-24 hours.
Beat drained cheese until smooth. Mix in salt and wasabi to taste.
Adjust wasabi - it fades slightly over time.
Refrigerate. Best within 2 weeks.

notes: Real wasabi is expensive and subtle; prepared wasabi (horseradish-based) is hotter
Wasabi heat dissipates faster than chile heat
Classic pairing with smoked salmon on bagels

recipes.title: Miso Aged Gouda
recipes.source_note: Dutch Gouda with white miso paste for deep umami.
recipes.description: Aged Gouda enhanced with white miso paste, creating unprecedented umami depth. The fermented soybean paste amplifies Gouda's natural caramel notes.

instructions.text: Make standard Gouda through draining stage.
Mix miso paste into curds - it will add salt so reduce cheese salt.
Press and brief brine (reduce time due to miso salt).
Age at 55°F for 4-8 months for deep flavor development.
Miso's enzymes create unique aged character.

notes: White miso is milder and sweeter than red miso
Miso adds glutamates (umami) that deepen with aging
Revolutionary fusion - two fermented traditions meet

recipes.title: Thai Chile Cream Cheese
recipes.source_note: Cream cheese with Thai bird's eye chiles and lime.
recipes.description: Rich cream cheese with fiery Thai bird's eye chiles and lime zest. Bright, intense heat balanced by creamy richness - Southeast Asian inspiration.

instructions.text: Make standard cream cheese base.
After draining, beat until smooth.
Mince Thai chiles very finely (wear gloves - these are 50,000-100,000 Scoville).
Fold in chiles, lime zest, salt, and optional cilantro.
Refrigerate. Heat intensifies overnight.

notes: Bird's eye chiles are very hot - start with fewer and add to taste
Lime zest brightens and balances the heat
Excellent with rice crackers or in spring roll wrappers

recipes.title: Lemongrass Cream Cheese
recipes.source_note: Cream cheese infused with fresh lemongrass.
recipes.description: Light, aromatic cream cheese infused with fresh lemongrass. Citrusy and floral without being overpowering - a unique Southeast Asian twist.

instructions.text: Bruise lemongrass stalks and cut into 2-inch pieces.
Heat cream and milk to 160°F with lemongrass. Steep 30 minutes off heat.
Strain out lemongrass. Cool milk to 75°F.
Add starter and rennet. Let set 12-24 hours.
Drain 12-24 hours. Beat until smooth, add salt.
Refrigerate. Flavor develops over 1-2 days.

notes: Use only the pale lower portion of lemongrass stalks
Bruising releases essential oils
Pairs beautifully with tropical fruits and seafood

recipes.title: Wara (Nigerian Fresh Cheese)
recipes.source_note: West African soft cheese made by Fulani herders, coagulated with plant extract.
recipes.description: Traditional Nigerian soft cheese made by Fulani herders. Coagulated with calotropis plant juice, it has a unique slightly bitter edge and soft, tofu-like texture.

ingredients.item: calotropis leaf extract (or lemon juice substitute)

instructions.text: Heat milk to 185°F (85°C), stirring constantly.
Remove from heat. Add coagulant slowly while stirring.
Let stand 15-20 minutes until curds form.
Ladle curds into woven basket or cheesecloth-lined mold.
Press lightly with weight for 2-3 hours.
Unmold and salt lightly. Best eaten same day.

notes: Traditional coagulant is extract from Sodom apple (calotropis) plant
Lemon juice creates similar texture without the slight bitterness
Often fried in palm oil until golden - called 'wara elede'

missing_inputs: 1/4 cup calotropis leaf extract (or lemon juice substitute)

recipes.title: Klila (Moroccan Dried Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Moroccan dried cheese balls, traditional Berber preservation method.
recipes.description: Moroccan dried cheese made by Berber communities. Fresh cheese is salted, shaped into balls, and sun-dried for long preservation. Reconstituted in stews or eaten as snack.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 180°F (82°C). Add buttermilk, stir once.
Let curds form 10 minutes. Pour into cheesecloth.
Drain thoroughly 4-6 hours until quite dry.
Knead in salt. Form into small balls (golf ball sized).
Sun dry on clean cloth 3-7 days, turning daily, until completely hard.
Store in cool, dry place. Lasts months.

notes: Traditional Berber cheese preservation technique
Reconstitute in warm water or add directly to tagines
Can be grated over couscous when dried

missing_inputs: 1 gallon fresh goat or cow milk

recipes.title: Akkawi (Levantine Brine Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Brined white cheese from the Levant, named after Acre (Akka), Palestine.
recipes.description: Mild, white brined cheese from the Levant. Soft texture with moderate saltiness, traditionally desalted before use in sweets like knafeh or eaten fresh.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet, let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir 15 minutes, keeping temperature at 90°F.
Drain and press lightly (5 lbs) for 2 hours.
Cut into blocks and place in brine (1 lb salt per gallon water).
Age in brine 1-2 weeks refrigerated.

notes: Must be desalted in water 6-12 hours before using in desserts
Essential cheese for knafeh and other Middle Eastern sweets
Named after the ancient port city of Acre

recipes.title: Nabulsi (Palestinian Boiled Cheese)
recipes.source_note: White brined cheese from Nablus, Palestine. Traditionally boiled with mahlab and mastic.
recipes.description: Palestinian brined cheese from Nablus, distinctively flavored with mahlab (cherry pit spice) and mastic. Boiled preparation gives unique texture and flavor profile.

instructions.text: Make basic white cheese: heat milk to 90°F, add starter, ripen, add rennet.
Cut curds, drain, and press lightly for 2 hours.
Cut into rectangular blocks.
Boil cheese blocks in whey with mahlab and mastic for 30 minutes.
Cool and place in strong brine solution.
Age in brine 2-3 weeks.

notes: Mahlab adds distinctive cherry/almond flavor
Mastic provides subtle pine/resin notes
Boiling process creates characteristic squeaky texture

recipes.title: Rushan (Chinese Fan Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Stretched cheese from Yunnan Province, made by the Bai minority people.
recipes.description: Unique Chinese cheese from Yunnan's Bai people. Fresh cheese is stretched into thin sheets, dried on bamboo frames into fan shapes. Grilled or fried as street food.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 160°F (71°C).
Add sour whey or vinegar. Stir until curds form.
Collect curds, knead while still warm.
Stretch the warm curd repeatedly until smooth and elastic.
Shape into thin sheets and drape over bamboo sticks to form fan shape.
Dry until firm but still pliable. Grill over flame to serve.

notes: One of China's few traditional cheeses
Bai minority specialty from Dali region, Yunnan
Grilled rushan is popular Yunnan street food, often sweetened

missing_inputs: 1 cup sour whey or dilute vinegar

recipes.title: Rubing (Yunnan Goat Cheese)
recipes.attribution: Traditional Bai and Sani minority cheese
recipes.source_note: Firm goat milk cheese from Yunnan, made by Bai and Sani peoples.
recipes.description: Firm, mild goat cheese from Yunnan Province. Dense texture holds up to grilling or frying. Often served with chili flakes as a snack or appetizer.

instructions.text: Heat goat milk to 180°F (82°C), stirring to prevent scorching.
Remove from heat. Add sour whey or vinegar gradually while stirring.
Let curds form 10-15 minutes.
Drain curds in cheesecloth. Press in square mold with moderate weight.
Press 2-4 hours until firm block forms.
Unmold and salt surfaces. Ready to grill or fry.

notes: Sani and Bai peoples have made this cheese for centuries
Cut into cubes and pan-fry until golden outside, soft inside
Serve with Yunnan chili flakes and mint

recipes.title: Chhurpi (Himalayan Hard Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Rock-hard yak or cow milk cheese from Nepal, Bhutan, Tibet, and Sikkim.
recipes.description: Extremely hard Himalayan cheese, traditionally from yak milk. So hard it must be chewed for hours or softened in tea. Traditional protein source for mountain peoples.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 180°F (82°C). Add buttermilk to curdle.
Let curds form, then drain thoroughly in cloth.
Press curds very firmly for 24-48 hours.
Cut into small cubes or sticks.
Smoke over wood fire for several hours (traditional method).
Sun dry for 4-8 weeks until rock hard.

notes: So hard it's sometimes called 'Himalayan chewing gum'
Traditional long-lasting protein source for herders
Now popular as long-lasting dog chews internationally

recipes.title: Brânză de Burduf (Romanian Bark Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Romanian sheep cheese aged in fir bark or sheep stomach, from Transylvania.
recipes.description: Traditional Transylvanian sheep cheese, aged in pine bark cylinders or sheep stomach. Strong, pungent flavor with slight resinous notes from the bark. A mountain shepherd specialty.

instructions.text: Make basic sheep cheese: heat milk to 95°F, add starter, rennet, form curds.
Drain and press curds until quite dry.
Crumble or grate the pressed cheese finely.
Mix thoroughly with salt.
Pack tightly into bark cylinder or sheep stomach.
Age in cool cellar 2-4 weeks.

notes: Burduf means the bark container or sheep stomach casing
Fir bark imparts subtle resinous, forest character
Protected Traditional Specialty in Romania

recipes.title: Sulguni (Georgian Stretched Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Georgian brined cheese with layered, stringy texture from Samegrelo region.
recipes.description: Iconic Georgian cheese with distinctive layered, stringy texture from stretching. Brined in salt water, it's mild with slight sourness. Often smoked for deeper flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F (35°C). Add starter, ripen 45 minutes.
Add rennet, let set 45 minutes.
Cut curds, let acidify at room temperature 6-12 hours.
When curds stretch smoothly in 170°F water, proceed to stretching.
Heat curds in 170°F (77°C) water, stretch and fold repeatedly.
Form into rounds, cool in ice water. Brine 1-2 weeks.

notes: Similar to mozzarella but acidified longer for tangier flavor
Smoked sulguni (shemtsvari) is a Megrelian specialty
Essential filling for khachapuri (Georgian cheese bread)

recipes.title: Rum Washed Gouda
recipes.source_note: Dutch Gouda with Caribbean rum washes for tropical character.
recipes.description: Creamy Dutch Gouda enhanced with Caribbean rum washes during aging. Caramel, vanilla, and molasses notes from the rum complement Gouda's natural sweetness.

instructions.text: Make standard Gouda with washed-curd method.
Brine as normal, then air dry 3-4 days.
Begin rum washes: brush entire surface with rum every 3-4 days.
Continue rum washes for 6 weeks.
Age at 55°F for 3-6 months total.

notes: Use quality aged rum for best flavor
Molasses and caramel notes develop from the rum
Excellent with tropical fruits and dark chocolate

recipes.title: Tequila Washed Queso
recipes.source_note: Mexican-style cheese washed with reposado tequila.
recipes.description: Mexican semi-firm cheese enhanced with reposado tequila washes. Agave and oak notes from the tequila create a distinctly Mexican cheese with complex character.

instructions.text: Make semi-firm Mexican-style cheese base.
Press, brine briefly, and air dry 3 days.
Wash with tequila every 3-4 days for 4-6 weeks.
Age at 55°F for 2-4 months total.

notes: Reposado tequila adds oak and agave complexity
Añejo tequila creates even deeper, woodier flavor
Perfect for elevated quesadillas and Mexican dishes

recipes.title: Szechuan Peppercorn Jack
recipes.source_note: Monterey Jack with Szechuan peppercorns for numbing heat.
recipes.description: Creamy Monterey Jack with Szechuan peppercorns' distinctive numbing, citrusy sensation. Unique 'ma la' effect creates tingles unlike any other cheese.

instructions.text: Lightly toast and crush Szechuan peppercorns - don't grind to powder.
Make standard Monterey Jack base.
Mix crushed peppercorns into drained curds with salt.
Press and age as standard Jack cheese 4-8 weeks.

notes: Szechuan peppercorns create numbing sensation, not spicy heat
Citrus and floral notes complement mild Jack cheese
Excellent in fusion dishes or with Asian pears

recipes.title: Dukkah Coated Chèvre
recipes.source_note: Fresh goat cheese rolled in Egyptian dukkah nut-spice blend.
recipes.description: Creamy fresh goat cheese rolled in Egyptian dukkah - a blend of hazelnuts, coriander, cumin, and sesame. Crunchy coating with Middle Eastern aromatics.

instructions.text: Make standard fresh chèvre.
Drain 24 hours until thick and shapeable.
Form into log shape. Salt lightly.
Roll log firmly in dukkah, coating completely.
Refrigerate 24 hours for flavors to meld.
Slice into rounds to serve.

notes: Dukkah is Egyptian nut-spice blend with hazelnuts, coriander, cumin, sesame
Crunchy coating contrasts with creamy cheese
Serve with olive oil and warm flatbread

recipes.title: Everything Bagel Cream Cheese
recipes.source_note: Cream cheese mixed with everything bagel seasoning.
recipes.description: Homemade cream cheese loaded with everything bagel seasoning - poppy seeds, sesame seeds, dried garlic, dried onion, and coarse salt. A deli classic made at home.

instructions.text: Make standard cream cheese base.
Drain 12-24 hours until thick.
Beat until smooth.
Mix in salt and everything bagel seasoning thoroughly.
Refrigerate to firm up before serving.

notes: Everything seasoning includes poppy, sesame, garlic, onion, salt
A New York deli staple
Perfect on fresh bagels or crackers

recipes.title: Piri Piri Cream Cheese
recipes.source_note: Cream cheese with African bird's eye chili (piri piri).
recipes.description: Cream cheese infused with piri piri - the African bird's eye chili used in Portuguese-African cuisine. Bright, sharp heat with citrus notes.

instructions.text: Make standard cream cheese base and drain.
Beat until smooth.
Mix in salt, piri piri, and lemon zest.
Adjust heat level to taste.
Refrigerate overnight for flavors to develop.

notes: Piri piri chili originated in Africa, adopted by Portuguese colonizers
Heat level varies - adjust to taste
Excellent with grilled chicken or on crusty bread

missing_inputs: 2 tbsp piri piri sauce or paste

recipes.title: Black Garlic Brie
recipes.source_note: Creamy Brie with caramelized black garlic for umami depth.
recipes.description: Creamy Brie-style cheese with sweet, caramelized black garlic folded throughout. Deep umami notes without raw garlic's pungency - sophisticated and complex.

instructions.text: Make Brie base: heat milk to 90°F, add cultures, ripen, add rennet.
Cut curds, drain gently into Brie molds.
Flip several times over 24 hours.
Salt all surfaces. Mash black garlic and spread on top surface.
Age at 55°F and 90%+ humidity. White bloom will develop.
Ready when soft throughout, about 4-6 weeks.

notes: Black garlic is sweet, mild, and umami-rich - no raw garlic bite
Can also fold black garlic into center for stuffed effect
Pairs with crusty bread and fig preserves

recipes.title: Matcha Green Tea Cream Cheese
recipes.source_note: Cream cheese with ceremonial grade matcha green tea.
recipes.description: Silky cream cheese with ceremonial grade matcha, creating earthy, vegetal notes with subtle sweetness. Vibrant green color and sophisticated umami character.

instructions.text: Make standard cream cheese base and drain thoroughly.
Sift matcha to remove lumps.
Beat cream cheese until smooth.
Add sifted matcha, salt, and optional honey. Mix thoroughly.
Refrigerate overnight for color and flavor to develop.

notes: Use ceremonial grade matcha for best color and flavor
Culinary grade works but produces more bitter result
Beautiful on Asian-inspired pastries or with fruit

recipes.title: Brie de Meaux
recipes.source_note: Classic French cheesemaking tradition from Île-de-France region.
recipes.description: The king of cheeses - a soft-ripened cheese with bloomy white rind and creamy interior. AOC protected since 1980.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add mesophilic culture, P. candidum, and G. candidum. Stir gently and let ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk. Stir gently.
Add diluted rennet using up-and-down motion. Let set undisturbed 90 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently ladle curds into Brie molds (8-inch diameter) lined on draining mat. Fill to top - curds will reduce.
Flip molds every 2-3 hours for first day. Let drain at room temperature (72°F) for 24 hours.
Remove from mold. Salt all surfaces evenly. Place on aging mat.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) with 90-95% humidity. Flip daily.
White mold should appear within 10-14 days. Continue aging 4-8 weeks until rind is fully developed and interior softens.

notes: Traditional Brie uses raw milk - pasteurized works but flavor differs
Proper humidity is critical for rind development
Cheese is ripe when it yields to gentle pressure
Best at room temperature - remove from fridge 1 hour before serving

missing_inputs: 1/4 tsp mesophilic culture (Flora Danica or MM100)

recipes.title: Comté (French Gruyère)
recipes.source_note: AOC protected cheese from the Jura mountains since 1958.
recipes.description: A pressed, cooked cheese with complex nutty, fruity flavors that deepen with age. France's most popular cheese.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add thermophilic culture and Propionibacterium. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add rennet diluted in cool water. Stir gently. Let set 30-40 minutes until firm.
Cut curd into rice-sized pieces (1/4 inch). Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat curds to 130°F (54°C) over 45 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent matting.
Hold at temperature, stirring, until curds are firm and squeaky (about 45 minutes).
Drain whey. Transfer curds to large wheel mold (10-12 inch). Press at 25 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 50 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine in saturated salt solution at 50°F for 24 hours (12 hours per pound).
Air dry 2-3 days until rind forms.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 90% humidity. Wash rind with brine weekly. Flip twice weekly.
After 3 months, move to warmer cave (65°F) for 3 weeks to develop eyes. Return to 55°F.
Minimum aging 4 months, ideal 12-24 months.

notes: Traditional wheels weigh 80-100 lbs - this is scaled for home use
Copper vats are traditional and contribute to flavor
Eyes should be size of cherries or smaller
Rind should be rubbed with oil or waxed if humidity is low

missing_inputs: as needed for brining cheese salt

recipes.title: Roquefort-Style Blue Cheese
recipes.source_note: AOC Roquefort must be aged in Combalou caves. This is a home adaptation.
recipes.description: The original blue cheese - tangy sheep's milk cheese with bold blue-green veins and crumbly texture.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F (30°C). Add mesophilic culture and P. roqueforti. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir for 30 minutes, maintaining temperature. Curds should firm slightly.
Drain whey. Let curds mat for 15 minutes.
Break up curds gently. Salt curds, mixing thoroughly.
Pack loosely into cylindrical mold, leaving air pockets. Do not press.
Flip several times over 24 hours. Let drain at room temperature.
Remove from mold. Salt exterior surfaces.
Age at 46-50°F (8-10°C) with 95% humidity. After 2 weeks, pierce with sterile needle to create air channels for blue growth.
Continue aging 3-6 months. Blue veins should develop within 4-6 weeks of piercing.

notes: True Roquefort must use milk from Lacaune sheep and age in specific caves
Sheep's milk gives characteristic tangy flavor
Can substitute cow or goat milk but character will differ
Pierce in a crosshatch pattern for even blue distribution

recipes.title: Camembert de Normandie
recipes.source_note: AOC protected. Created around 1791 by Marie Harel in Normandy.
recipes.description: Classic soft-ripened cheese with white bloomy rind. Smaller and more intense than Brie.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add mesophilic culture and mold cultures. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Ladle curds gently into Camembert molds (4.5-inch diameter). Fill to top.
Flip molds every 2-3 hours for the first day. Drain at 72°F.
After 24 hours, remove from molds. Salt all surfaces.
Place on aging mat. Age at 50-55°F with 90-95% humidity.
Flip daily. White mold appears in 7-10 days.
Age 3-5 weeks until rind is fully covered and interior softens.

notes: Traditional Camembert uses ladle-cut curds for creamier texture
Ripe when center yields to gentle pressure
Overripe will have ammonia smell
Serve in traditional wooden box at room temperature

recipes.title: Chèvre Bûchette (Goat Log)
recipes.source_note: Classic French fresh goat cheese in log form.
recipes.description: A fresh, tangy goat cheese formed into a log shape, often coated with herbs or ash.

instructions.text: Heat goat's milk to 72°F (22°C) - room temperature.
Add culture and stir gently. Let ripen 30 minutes.
Add just 2 drops rennet diluted in 2 tbsp water. Stir briefly.
Cover and let set 12-24 hours at 72°F until thick like yogurt.
Gently ladle curd into cheesecloth-lined colander.
Let drain 12-24 hours until desired consistency.
Add salt and mix gently.
Form into logs using plastic wrap or mold.
Roll in herbs, ash, or leave plain.
Refrigerate. Best within 2 weeks fresh.

notes: Very little rennet - this is primarily acid-set
Longer draining = firmer cheese
Can age with bloomy rind by adding P. candidum
Classic coating combinations: herbs, ash, cracked pepper

missing_inputs: 1/8 tsp mesophilic culture (Chèvre culture or C20G)

recipes.title: Crottin de Chavignol
recipes.source_note: AOC protected since 1976. From the Sancerre wine region.
recipes.description: Small, drum-shaped goat cheese that hardens with age. Name means 'little dropping.'

instructions.text: Heat goat's milk to 68-72°F (20-22°C). Add culture (and P. candidum if aging).
Let ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet drops diluted in 1 tbsp water.
Let set 24 hours until very firm curd.
Gently ladle into small cylindrical molds (2-inch diameter).
Let drain 2-3 days, flipping twice daily.
Remove from molds. Salt all surfaces.
Fresh (mi-sec): eat at 2 weeks. Blue (bleu): 4-8 weeks. Repassed (repassé): 12+ weeks.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) with 80% humidity.

notes: Four stages: fresh (8 days), mi-sec (2 weeks), bleu (1 month), repassé (3+ months)
Aged versions become very hard and sharp
Classic pairing with Sancerre wine
Warm crottin salad is traditional preparation

recipes.title: Mesost (Norwegian Whey Cheese)
recipes.description: A sweet, caramelized brown cheese made from whey. Called Brunost's predecessor.

instructions.text: Strain whey through cheesecloth to remove any curd particles.
Pour whey into large heavy-bottomed pot. Add cream and milk.
Bring to boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat and simmer, stirring frequently to prevent scorching.
Continue cooking 4-6 hours until reduced to thick paste and caramel brown.
Stir constantly in final hour as mixture thickens.
Pour into greased mold or container.
Cool completely. Refrigerate. Slice thin to serve.

notes: Uses whey otherwise discarded from cheesemaking
Lactose caramelizes during long cooking
Traditional served on Norwegian flatbread
Goat whey makes authentic Geitost flavor

recipes.title: Milawa Blue-Style Cheese
recipes.source_note: Inspired by Victoria's Milawa Cheese Company tradition.
recipes.description: An Australian-style blue cheese with creamy texture and mild blue flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 88°F (31°C). Add cultures. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir for 30 minutes at temperature.
Drain whey. Salt curds and mix gently.
Pack loosely into cylindrical mold, leaving air gaps.
Flip daily for 3 days at room temperature.
Pierce with sterile needle after 2 weeks.
Age at 50°F (10°C) with 95% humidity for 2-3 months.

notes: Australian blue cheeses tend to be milder than European
Creamy rather than crumbly texture
Good introduction to blue cheese making
Wrap in foil during aging to retain moisture

recipes.title: Valdeón Blue Cheese
recipes.source_note: PGI protected. From the Picos de Europa mountains.
recipes.description: A bold Spanish blue cheese wrapped in sycamore leaves, made from cow and goat milk blend.

ingredients.item: sycamore or maple leaves (optional, for wrapping)

instructions.text: Combine milks. Heat to 86°F (30°C). Add cultures. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 3/4-inch cubes. Rest 15 minutes.
Gently stir for 30 minutes, maintaining temperature.
Drain whey. Let curds mat 20 minutes.
Break up curds. Salt and mix.
Pack loosely into tall cylindrical mold.
Flip daily for 4-5 days at room temperature.
Pierce extensively after 3 weeks.
Age at 46-50°F (8-10°C) with 95% humidity.
Wrap in blanched leaves at 2 months. Continue aging 3-4 months total.

notes: Mixed milk gives complex flavor
Leaf wrapping is traditional presentation
Should be intensely blue and piquant
Similar to Cabrales but slightly milder

recipes.title: Kalari (Kashmiri Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Ancient cheese from the Jammu region of Kashmir.
recipes.description: A dense, chewy cheese traditionally made from buffalo milk, perfect for frying.

ingredients.item: whole buffalo milk (or whole cow's milk)

instructions.text: Heat milk to 180°F (82°C) in heavy pot.
Add sour whey or yogurt. Stir gently.
Let curds form and separate from whey.
Drain through cheesecloth. Squeeze out excess whey.
Knead curds while still warm, incorporating salt.
Form into thick disc or oval shape.
Let cool and firm up at room temperature.
Can be stored in brine or dried for preservation.

notes: Buffalo milk gives authentic dense texture
Traditionally fried until golden and served hot
Similar texture to halloumi
Called 'maish krej' when smoked

recipes.title: Leyden Cheese (Dutch Cumin Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Historic cheese from Leiden, Netherlands. Bears city's coat of arms.
recipes.description: A semi-hard Dutch cheese flavored with cumin and sometimes caraway seeds.

instructions.text: Skim some cream from milk to reduce fat. Add buttermilk. Heat to 88°F (31°C).
Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Replace with hot water to wash curds. Raise temp to 102°F (39°C).
Stir for 30 minutes until curds firm.
Drain whey. Mix in cumin (and caraway) and salt.
Pack into wheel mold. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, 40 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine for 12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Age at 55°F (13°C) with 85% humidity for 2-6 months.
Rub with oil or wax to prevent cracking.

notes: Traditionally made from partially skimmed milk
Buttermilk adds tang and helps culture
Cumin should be visible throughout cheese
Authentic wheels are stamped with crossed keys of Leiden

recipes.title: Queso de Bola (Mexican Ball Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Historic cheese brought by Dutch traders, adapted in Mexico.
recipes.description: A Mexican adaptation of Edam cheese, encased in red wax. Key ingredient in queso relleno.

instructions.text: Remove some cream from milk. Heat to 90°F (32°C).
Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Slowly heat to 102°F (39°C), stirring gently for 30 minutes.
Remove 1/3 whey and add warm water (washing curds).
Continue stirring until curds are firm and squeaky.
Drain and salt curds. Pack into ball mold.
Press at 25 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine for 12-24 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Age at 55°F for 2-4 months.
Coat in red wax before final aging or selling.

notes: Based on Dutch Edam brought in colonial era
Essential for Yucatecan queso relleno
Red wax is traditional coating
Mild, slightly nutty flavor

recipes.title: Traditional Welsh Caerphilly
recipes.source_note: Historic miners' cheese from Caerphilly, South Wales.
recipes.description: A crumbly, moist cheese with lemony tang. Quick to make, designed for Welsh coal miners.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 95°F (35°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Let curds settle. Drain most whey.
Pile curds, let drain 10 min, then mill into small pieces.
Salt milled curds. Mix well.
Pack into mold. Press at 10 lbs for 10 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8 hours or dry salt rind.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 85% humidity for 2-8 weeks.

notes: Quick-aging cheese - can eat at 2 weeks
Higher moisture than most British cheeses
Crumbly texture is characteristic
Provided miners with high-salt cheese for replenishment

recipes.title: Double Gloucester Cheese
recipes.source_note: Historic English territorial cheese from Gloucestershire.
recipes.description: A firm, mellow cheese with buttery flavor, traditionally made from full-fat Gloucester cattle milk.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add annatto if using for golden color.
Add culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F (38°C) over 40 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold and stir until curds are very firm.
Drain whey. Let curds mat, then mill into small pieces.
Salt curds. Let rest 10 minutes.
Pack into mold. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 40 lbs for 24 hours.
Bandage wrap with cheesecloth and lard.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 85% humidity for 3-6 months.

notes: Double refers to full-fat milk, not thickness
Single Gloucester uses partially skimmed milk
Famous for cheese rolling at Cooper's Hill
Smooth, close texture when aged properly

recipes.title: Sage Derby Cheese
recipes.source_note: Historic English herb cheese, traditionally made for Christmas.
recipes.description: A mild, smooth cheese marbled with green sage leaves, traditionally served at Christmas.

instructions.text: Blanch sage in boiling water 30 seconds. Drain and chop fine.
Make spinach juice by blending spinach with small amount of water and straining.
Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 95°F (35°C), stirring gently for 40 minutes.
Drain whey. Divide curds in half.
Mix sage and spinach juice into one half of curds.
Salt both portions of curds.
Layer white and green curds in mold, creating marbled effect.
Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, then 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 85% humidity for 1-3 months.

notes: Traditionally made for Christmas
Spinach juice maintains green color (sage alone turns brown)
Mild cheese lets sage flavor shine
Modern versions sometimes use chlorophyll for color

recipes.title: Cornish Yarg (Nettle-Wrapped Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Historic cheese revived by Alan Gray (Yarg = Gray backwards).
recipes.description: A creamy, crumbly cheese wrapped in nettle leaves that impart earthy, mushroom notes.

instructions.text: If using fresh nettles, blanch briefly and dry (wear gloves!).
Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 60 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F (38°C), stirring gently for 30 minutes.
Drain whey. Salt curds and mix.
Pack into mold. Press at 15 lbs for 30 min, then 30 lbs for 6 hours.
Remove from mold. Apply nettle leaves to cover entire surface.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) with 90% humidity for 4-8 weeks.
Nettles develop blue-gray mold; this is normal and desired.

notes: Nettles lose sting when dried or blanched
Mold growing through nettles creates lacy pattern
Interior becomes creamy under the rind
Wild Garlic Yarg uses ramsons instead of nettles

recipes.title: Dunlop Cheese (Scottish Cheddar)
recipes.source_note: Historic cheese from Dunlop, Ayrshire. Scotland's original cheddar-style.
recipes.description: A mild, buttery Scottish cheese, softer and sweeter than English cheddar.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F (38°C) over 40 minutes, stirring gently.
Let curds settle. Drain whey.
Cut curd mass into slabs. Stack and flip every 15 minutes for 1 hour.
Mill curds. Salt and mix well.
Pack into mold. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, then 40 lbs for 24 hours.
Bandage wrap or wax.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 85% humidity for 2-6 months.

notes: Originated in 1688 by Barbara Gilmour
Milder and moister than English cheddar
Ayrshire cattle milk gives distinctive richness
Less acidic than cheddar due to shorter cheddaring

recipes.title: Bergkäse (Austrian Mountain Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Alpine cheese tradition from Austrian mountain dairies.
recipes.description: A firm, nutty Alpine cheese similar to Gruyère but with distinctive Austrian character.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add cultures. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd into rice-sized pieces (1/4 inch).
Slowly heat to 125°F (52°C) over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at temperature, stirring, until curds are firm (30-45 minutes).
Let curds settle. Drain whey.
Transfer to large wheel mold (10-inch). Press at 25 lbs for 30 min, then 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Brine in saturated solution for 24-48 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 90% humidity. Wash rind with brine weekly.
Minimum aging 6 months, ideal 12-18 months.

notes: Made from milk of cows grazing Alpine pastures
Cooked curd technique similar to Gruyère
Eyes should be small and well-distributed
Flavor develops complexity over long aging

missing_inputs: as needed for brining cheese salt

recipes.title: Olomoucké Tvarůžky (Czech Ripened Cheese)
recipes.source_note: PGI protected. Only Czech cheese with EU protection.
recipes.description: A pungent, surface-ripened cheese made from sour milk curd. Czech national cheese.

instructions.text: Start with fresh quark. Let it ripen at room temperature 3-7 days until it develops strong aroma.
Knead ripened curd thoroughly with salt (and caraway if using).
Form into small disc shapes, about 1 inch thick and 2 inches diameter.
Place on mat and let dry slightly for 24 hours.
Move to ripening chamber at 55-60°F (13-15°C) with 90% humidity.
Turn daily. Surface will become sticky and develop yellow-orange color.
Ripen 2-6 weeks depending on desired intensity.
Cheese is ready when soft throughout and very aromatic.

recipes.temperature: Room temp for initial ripening; 55-60°F (13-15°C) for aging
notes: One of the world's smelliest cheeses
No rennet used - purely acid-set
Traditional eaten with bread, onions, and beer
Younger cheese is milder; aged is very intense

recipes.title: Bundz (Polish Highland Fresh Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Fresh sheep's milk cheese from Tatra Mountain highlanders.
recipes.description: A fresh, mild sheep's milk cheese from the Polish highlands. Base for smoked oscypek.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 95°F (35°C).
Add rennet diluted in small amount of water. Stir briefly.
Let set 30-45 minutes until firm curd.
Break up curd with hands in pot.
Drain whey through cheesecloth.
Salt curds and mix.
Pack into small mold or form by hand.
Eat fresh within 3-5 days, or press and smoke to make oscypek.

notes: Base cheese for oscypek when pressed and smoked
Must be sheep's milk for authentic flavor
Fresh bundz is mild and slightly tangy
Traditional part of highlander shepherding culture

recipes.title: Leipäjuusto (Finnish Bread Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Also called juustoleipä. Traditionally made from reindeer or cow colostrum.
recipes.description: A fresh, squeaky baked cheese with caramelized surface. Traditionally served with cloudberry jam.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 100°F (38°C). Add buttermilk. Stir.
Add rennet diluted in 2 tbsp water. Let set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently stir for 10 minutes. Drain whey.
Salt curds. Press into flat disc shape in oven-safe pan.
Bake under broiler 5-7 minutes until top is spotted golden-brown.
Flip and broil other side.
Serve warm with cloudberry jam or coffee.

notes: Traditional uses colostrum (first milk after calving)
Squeaky texture is characteristic
Can be dried and stored, then reconstituted in cream
Called 'Finnish squeaky cheese' in US markets

recipes.title: Traditional Skyr (Icelandic Fresh Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Viking-era cultured dairy product, technically a fresh cheese not yogurt.
recipes.description: A thick, creamy cultured cheese similar to Greek yogurt but technically a fresh acid-set cheese.

ingredients.item: skyr or plain Greek yogurt (as starter)

instructions.text: Heat skim milk to 195°F (90°C). Hold 10 minutes.
Cool to 110°F (43°C).
Add starter (existing skyr or Greek yogurt). Mix well.
Add rennet drops diluted in 1 tbsp water.
Cover and keep at 110°F for 12-24 hours until very thick and tangy.
Line colander with fine cheesecloth. Pour in skyr.
Drain 4-8 hours until thick.
Beat until smooth. Traditionally served with cream and sugar.

notes: Technically a fresh cheese, not yogurt
Very high protein due to straining
Traditional uses skim milk, not whole
Must use skyr or similar starter - regular yogurt gives different result

recipes.title: Chechil (Armenian String Cheese)
recipes.description: A pulled, braided string cheese from Armenia. Often smoked and sold in braids.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F (35°C). Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 105°F (40°C), stirring gently.
Drain whey. Let curds acidify at room temperature 4-8 hours until stretchy.
Heat water to 170°F (77°C). Add curds.
Stretch and pull into long thin strings.
Braid or twist strings together.
Salt in brine for 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Optional: Cold smoke for 2-4 hours for traditional smoked chechil.

notes: Similar to mozzarella technique but stretched into strings
Must acidify enough to stretch properly
Smoked version is most traditional
Popular snack cheese in Caucasus region

recipes.title: Raclette du Valais (Traditional Swiss Melting Cheese)
recipes.source_note: AOC protected Swiss Alpine cheese for melting.
recipes.description: The original melting cheese from Valais, Switzerland. Made to be scraped onto potatoes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 104°F (40°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Continue stirring at temperature until curds are firm but still moist.
Drain whey. Pack into large wheel mold (12-inch diameter).
Press at 30 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 50 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine in saturated solution for 24-48 hours.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 92% humidity for 3-6 months.
Wash rind with brine 2-3 times weekly. Rind becomes light brown.

notes: Designed specifically for melting
Should become creamy and aromatic when heated
Traditional served scraped from half-wheel onto potatoes
Rind washing develops flavor complexity

recipes.title: Provolone Piccante (Aged Sharp Provolone)
recipes.source_note: DOP protected. Aged pasta filata cheese with pronounced sharp flavor.
recipes.description: Sharp, aged provolone with piquant flavor from goat or lamb rennet. Aged minimum 4 months.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 97°F (36°C). Dissolve lipase in 1/4 cup water, add to milk.
Add thermophilic culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 118°F (48°C) over 30 minutes, stirring continuously.
Drain whey. Let curds acidify at room temp until pH 5.2 (stretchy test).
Heat water to 175°F (80°C). Add curds in portions.
Stretch and fold until smooth. Form into pear or sausage shape.
Tie with raffia or string. Plunge in cold water to set shape.
Brine for 12-24 hours depending on size.
Hang to dry 2 weeks at 55°F with good air circulation.
Age minimum 4 months, up to 12+ months for extra sharp.

recipes.temperature: 97-118°F (36-48°C) for make; 175°F (80°C) for stretching; 55°F (13°C) for aging
notes: Goat or lamb rennet gives characteristic piquant flavor
Lipase adds sharpness
Piccante means aged minimum 4 months
Traditional shapes: pear (pera), salami, giant (mandarone)

recipes.title: Manchego Artesano (Artisan La Mancha Cheese)
recipes.source_note: DOP protected. Spain's most famous cheese from Manchega sheep.
recipes.description: The quintessential Spanish sheep's milk cheese with distinctive herringbone pattern on rind.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F (30°C). Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces (rice-sized).
Slowly heat to 104°F (40°C) over 30 minutes, stirring continuously.
Hold at temperature and stir until curds are very firm.
Drain whey. Pack curds into traditional pleita mold (with zigzag pattern) or plain mold.
Press at 20 lbs for 1 hour, flip, then 30 lbs for 8-12 hours.
Remove and salt all surfaces, or brine 24 hours.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) with 85% humidity.
Rub with olive oil weekly. Turn twice weekly.
Fresco: 2 weeks. Semi-curado: 3-6 months. Curado: 6-12 months. Viejo: 12+ months.

notes: True Manchego uses only Manchega sheep milk
Herringbone pattern from traditional esparto grass molds
Olive oil rubbing creates characteristic rind
Flavor ranges from mild (fresco) to intense (viejo)

recipes.title: Graviera Kritis (Cretan Gruyère)
recipes.source_note: PDO protected. Greek version of Gruyère made primarily from sheep's milk.
recipes.description: A hard, nutty cheese from Crete with sweet, caramelized notes. Greece's second most popular cheese.

instructions.text: Combine milks. Heat to 95°F (35°C). Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 40 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces.
Slowly heat to 125°F (52°C) over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at temperature, stirring until curds are firm and squeaky.
Drain whey. Pack into wheel mold.
Press at 25 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Brine in saturated solution for 24-48 hours.
Air dry 3-5 days.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 85% humidity for 5-12 months.
Rub with olive oil monthly. Turn twice weekly.

notes: Primarily sheep's milk with some goat
Cooked curd technique similar to Swiss Gruyère
Should develop small eyes
Popular table cheese and for saganaki

recipes.title: Queijo Serra da Estrela
recipes.source_note: DOP protected. Portugal's most famous cheese, made with thistle rennet.
recipes.description: A rich, creamy sheep's cheese coagulated with cardoon thistle. The top is cut off and contents scooped.

instructions.text: Prepare thistle rennet: soak dried flowers in warm water for 2-3 hours. Strain and reserve liquid.
Heat sheep's milk to 85°F (29°C).
Add thistle infusion. Stir gently.
Let set 60-90 minutes until soft curd forms.
Gently break up curd with hands. Do not cut with knife.
Let curds settle. Drain some whey.
Ladle curds into cincho (belt-wrapped mold) or cloth-lined mold.
Press very lightly - just hand pressure, or up to 5 lbs.
Salt top surface. Flip after 12 hours and salt other side.
Age at 46-50°F (8-10°C) with 90% humidity for 4-8 weeks.
When ripe, interior should be nearly liquid. Cut top like a lid and scoop contents.

notes: Thistle rennet is essential for authentic flavor
Very soft, almost liquid interior when ripe
Traditional to cut off top and eat with spoon
Made only during winter lambing season traditionally

recipes.title: Beaufort d'Alpage (Summer Alpine Beaufort)
recipes.source_note: AOC protected. Made only during summer in high Alpine pastures.
recipes.description: The prince of Gruyères - a large, complex Alpine cheese made from summer mountain milk.

ingredients.item: whole cow's milk (raw, from Alpine pasture)

instructions.text: Heat milk to 91°F (33°C). Add culture. Ripen 20 minutes.
Add rennet. Let set 30 minutes until firm.
Cut curd into corn kernel-sized pieces.
Slowly heat to 130°F (54°C) over 45 minutes, stirring continuously.
Hold at temperature, stirring vigorously for 45-60 minutes until curds are very firm.
Transfer curds to traditional concave Beaufort mold with linen.
Press at 30 lbs for 30 min, flip repeatedly while pressing at 70 lbs for 20+ hours.
Traditional mold creates concave sides (distinctive Beaufort shape).
Brine in saturated solution for 48 hours.
Age at 50°F (10°C) with 95% humidity. Rub with brine twice weekly.
Minimum 5 months aging, optimal 12-24 months.

notes: Concave sides distinguish Beaufort from other Alpine cheeses
No eyes - should be smooth throughout
Summer milk from high pastures gives complex floral notes
Traditional wheels weigh 90-150 lbs

recipes.title: Taleggio DOP (Traditional Lombardy Washed-Rind)
recipes.source_note: DOP protected since 1996. Ancient cheese from Val Taleggio.
recipes.description: A soft, washed-rind cheese with thin pink-orange crust and mild, fruity, slightly tangy interior.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F (35°C). Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir for 20 minutes, maintaining temperature.
Drain whey. Ladle curds into square molds (6-8 inch).
Flip molds every 2 hours for first day at room temperature.
After 24 hours, remove from molds and salt all surfaces.
Age at 46-50°F (8-10°C) with 90-95% humidity.
Wash with brine every 2-3 days for first 3 weeks.
Continue aging 5-7 weeks. Rind becomes pink-orange, interior softens.

notes: Square shape is traditional and distinctive
Should have thin, sticky orange-pink rind
Interior becomes soft and oozy when perfectly ripe
Aroma is strong but flavor is surprisingly mild

recipes.title: Sbrinz (Swiss Extra-Hard Cheese)
recipes.source_note: AOC protected. Switzerland's oldest cheese, possibly 2000 years old.
recipes.description: An extremely hard, granular cheese aged 2-3 years. Swiss answer to Parmigiano-Reggiano.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture. Ripen 15 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 25 minutes.
Cut curd into very small rice-sized pieces (3mm).
Heat slowly to 135°F (57°C) over 60 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at temperature for 45-60 minutes until curds are very dry and sink.
Transfer to mold in one mass under whey. Press at 40 lbs immediately.
Press at 80 lbs for 24 hours, flipping several times.
Brine for 10-14 days, flipping daily.
Air dry 2 weeks at 65°F (18°C).
Age at 60°F (15°C) with 75-80% humidity for 18-36 months.
Oil rind occasionally to prevent cracking.

notes: Highest cooking temperature of any Swiss cheese
Must be aged minimum 18 months by law
Traditionally eaten in thin shavings (Hobelkäse)
Very low moisture - can be grated finely

recipes.title: Grana Padano
recipes.source_note: DOP protected. Sister cheese to Parmigiano-Reggiano from northern Italy.
recipes.description: A hard, granular Italian cheese similar to Parmesan but milder. Aged 9-24+ months.

instructions.text: Skim some cream from evening milk. Combine with morning milk.
Heat to 91°F (33°C). Add whey starter or culture. Ripen 15 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 12-15 minutes.
Break curd with spino (whisk) into rice-grain sized pieces.
Heat to 131°F (55°C) over 15 minutes, stirring constantly.
Let curds rest on bottom 45-60 minutes under whey.
Lift curd mass with cloth. Divide into two and place in molds.
Press with weights, flipping frequently for 2 days.
Brine in saturated solution for 14-30 days depending on size.
Age at 60-68°F (15-20°C) with 80-85% humidity.
Turn and brush weekly. Minimum 9 months, optimal 16-24 months.

Slightly milder than Parmigiano-Reggiano
Silage feeding allowed (not for Parmigiano)
Look for stamps: 9+ months, 16+ months (Riserva), 20+ months

recipes.title: Aged Gouda (48-Month Boerenkaas)
recipes.source_note: Farmhouse aged Gouda tradition from Netherlands.
recipes.description: Ultra-aged farmhouse Gouda with intense butterscotch, caramel notes and crunchy tyrosine crystals.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Replace with hot water (140°F) to raise temp to 100°F.
Stir gently for 30 minutes (curd washing develops sweet flavor).
Drain whey. Pack curds firmly into wheel mold.
Press at 20 lbs for 20 min, 40 lbs for 1 hour, then 50 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine in saturated solution for 24-48 hours.
Air dry 3-5 days until rind is dry.
Wax with multiple layers of cheese wax.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) with 85% humidity for 48 months.
Rewax if any cracks appear during aging.

notes: Curd washing removes lactose, creating sweeter aged flavor
Tyrosine crystals (white crunchy bits) develop with age
Raw milk essential for complex aged flavor
Color deepens to deep gold/amber with age

recipes.title: Stilton (British Blue Cheese)
recipes.source_note: PDO protected. Can only be made in Derbyshire, Leicestershire, and Nottinghamshire.
recipes.description: England's king of cheeses - a rich, creamy blue with complex, tangy flavor and ivory paste.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add mesophilic culture and P. roqueforti. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Let set 90 minutes until very firm.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 15 minutes.
Gently stir for 10 minutes only - do not heat.
Drain whey. Let curds drain in colander, turning hourly for 24 hours.
Mill curds into walnut-sized pieces. Salt thoroughly.
Pack loosely into tall cylindrical mold (7-inch diameter). No pressing.
Let drain at room temp 4-5 days, turning twice daily.
Remove from mold. Smooth sides with knife.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 90% humidity for 5 weeks before piercing.
Pierce with stainless needles to create air channels for blue.
Continue aging 9-12 weeks total. Turn twice weekly.

notes: Never pressed - texture comes from milling and natural consolidation
PDO requires pasteurized local milk
Natural rind develops crusty brown appearance
Traditionally eaten with port wine

recipes.title: Colby Cheese (Original Wisconsin Recipe)
recipes.source_note: American original, created in Colby, Wisconsin in 1885.
recipes.description: A mild, moist American cheese with open texture. Sweeter and softer than cheddar.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add annatto if using for orange color.
Add culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 3/8-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 102°F (39°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
COLBY WASH: Remove 1/3 whey. Add cold water to drop temp to 80°F (27°C).
Continue stirring 15 minutes. This stops acid development and creates moisture.
Drain. Salt curds while stirring to prevent matting.
Pack into mold. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, then 40 lbs for 4-6 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax or vacuum seal.
Age at 55°F (13°C) for 1-3 months.

notes: Cold water wash is key - stops acid development for sweeter flavor
Open, lacy texture is characteristic
Colby-Jack combines Colby with Monterey Jack
Moister than cheddar, doesn't age as long

recipes.title: Fromage Blanc (Fresh French Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Classic French fresh cheese, similar to quark or cream cheese.
recipes.description: A light, tangy fresh cheese perfect for spreading or desserts. Fat content varies by recipe.

instructions.text: Heat milk (and cream if using) to 72-77°F (22-25°C).
Add culture. Stir gently to distribute.
Add rennet drops diluted in 1 tbsp water. Stir briefly.
Cover and let culture 12-24 hours at room temperature until thick.
Gently ladle into cheesecloth-lined colander.
Let drain 6-12 hours until desired consistency.
Transfer to bowl. Add salt and beat until smooth.
Refrigerate. Use within 1-2 weeks.

notes: Adding cream makes it richer (like cream cheese)
Skim milk makes lighter, more tangy version
Can flavor with herbs, honey, or fruit
Very little rennet - primarily acid-set

recipes.title: Queso Fresco (Mexican Fresh Cheese)

instructions.text: Heat milk to 180°F (82°C), stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat. Add vinegar or lime juice. Stir gently.
Let sit 10-15 minutes until curds form and separate from whey.
Line colander with cheesecloth. Pour in curds.
Let drain 30 minutes.
Add salt to curds. Mix gently.
Press curds in cheesecloth or mold for 1-2 hours.
Refrigerate. Crumble to serve. Best within 1 week.

Does not melt - just softens when heated
Can be made with combination of milk and cream for richer version
Saltier versions are called queso seco

recipes.title: Shanklish (Lebanese Aged Cheese Balls)
recipes.source_note: Levantine aged cheese tradition, coated in za'atar and chili.
recipes.description: Fermented cheese balls coated with za'atar and Aleppo pepper. Aged until pungent.

instructions.text: If starting with yogurt, strain through cheesecloth 24-48 hours to make labneh.
Mix salt into labneh thoroughly.
Form into golf ball-sized spheres.
Place on rack and let dry at room temperature 2-3 days until surface is firm.
Mix za'atar, Aleppo pepper, and thyme.
Roll each ball in spice mixture, coating completely.
Place in jar. Age at room temperature 1-2 weeks for mild, 3-4 weeks for strong.
Store in olive oil to preserve. Will keep months refrigerated.

Served crumbled with tomatoes, onions, and olive oil
Pungent aroma is characteristic
Za'atar coating helps control mold growth

recipes.title: Sakura Cheese (Japanese-Style Blossom Cheese)

instructions.text: Rinse preserved sakura to remove excess salt. Set aside a few for garnish.
Steep remaining sakura in 1/4 cup hot milk for 15 minutes.
Heat milk and cream to 180°F (82°C).
Add vinegar and stir gently until curds form.
Add sakura-infused milk. Stir briefly.

Drain through cheesecloth-lined colander.
Add salt. Drain 4-24 hours depending on desired firmness.
Press into mold. Garnish top with reserved blossoms.

notes: Preserved sakura available at Japanese grocery stores
Subtle floral flavor, not overwhelming
Beautiful presentation for spring occasions

recipes.title: Chhena (Bengali Fresh Cheese)

recipes.title: Đậu Hũ Nóng (Vietnamese Fresh Soy Cheese)

recipes.title: Lor Peyniri (Turkish Whey Cheese)

recipes.title: Kajmak (Serbian Clotted Cream Cheese)

recipes.title: Sirene (Bulgarian White Cheese)

Crumbles when young, slices when aged

recipes.title: Chhurpi (Himalayan Hard Cheese)

recipes.title: Provoleta (Argentine Grilled Provolone)

recipes.title: Emmental (Classic Swiss Cheese with Eyes)

Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 105°F, stirring gently.
Let curds settle and acidify at 105°F until pH reaches 5.2-5.3 (2-4 hours).
Cut curd into strips. Stretch in 175-180°F water until smooth.
Form into pear shapes with a tied neck (traditional scamorza shape).
Cool in ice water for 15 minutes.
Brine for 2-3 hours in saturated salt solution.
Hang by strings to dry for 2-3 days in cool, airy place.
Cold smoke with wheat straw or fruit wood at 65-75°F for 2-4 hours.
Age hanging for 1-2 weeks before use.

recipes.temperature: 95-105°F for make; 175-180°F for stretching; 65-75°F for smoking
notes: The tied neck creates the traditional gourd shape
Scamorza is firmer than mozzarella due to the aging step
Excellent grilled as scamorza alla piastra

recipes.title: Smoked Idiazábal
recipes.source_note: PDO Basque sheep's milk cheese with beech and cherry wood smoke
recipes.description: Firm, buttery Basque sheep's milk cheese with intense smoky flavor from traditional cherry and beech smoking.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F. Add culture and ripen for 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 45-60 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise temperature to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 100°F for 30 minutes more until curds are firm.
Drain whey and press curds into molds at 15 lbs for 1 hour.
Flip and press at 30 lbs for 6-8 hours or overnight.
Dry salt by rubbing salt on all surfaces. Salt for 24 hours, turning once.
Air dry for 2-3 days until natural rind forms.
Age at 50-55°F for minimum 2 months.
Cold smoke with cherry and beech wood at 68-77°F for 8-12 hours over 2-3 days.
Continue aging for 2-6 months total for best flavor.

recipes.temperature: 86-100°F for make; 68-77°F for smoking; 50-55°F for aging
notes: Traditional Idiazábal uses Latxa or Carranzana sheep's milk
Beech and cherry wood are traditional for Basque smoking
The long, slow smoking is key to the intense smoke flavor
Natural rind develops a beautiful dark amber color from smoking

recipes.title: Ricotta Affumicata (Smoked Ricotta)
recipes.source_note: Sicilian and Calabrian smoked ricotta for grating
recipes.description: Dense, firm smoked ricotta with brown exterior, used for grating over pasta like ricotta salata but with smoky depth.

instructions.text: Heat fresh whey (and milk if using) to 185-195°F, stirring occasionally.
Add vinegar or lemon juice. Stir gently and watch for flocculation.
Remove from heat and let curds rise for 5-10 minutes.
Skim curds gently and place in ricotta basket or cheesecloth-lined mold.
Let drain at room temperature for 2-4 hours.
Salt all surfaces generously. Place in mold and weight lightly.
Refrigerate and drain for 2-3 days, salting surfaces daily.
Air dry at 55-60°F for 5-7 days until firm exterior develops.
Cold smoke with fruit wood at 65-75°F for 3-4 hours.
Continue aging at 55°F for 2-4 weeks. Grate like Parmesan over pasta.

recipes.temperature: 185-195°F for make; 65-75°F for smoking; 55°F for aging
notes: Use fresh whey within a few hours of cheesemaking for best yield
The longer you drain and salt, the firmer the final cheese
Excellent grated over pasta e fagioli or eggplant dishes

recipes.title: Smoked Blue Cheese
recipes.source_note: Modern American artisan smoked blue cheese technique
recipes.description: Creamy, tangy blue cheese with subtle cold smoke flavor that complements the Penicillium complexity.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture and P. roqueforti. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 90 minutes until firm.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently stir for 15 minutes at 86°F. Do not heat further.
Drain whey. Ladle curds gently into molds without pressing.
Let drain naturally, turning every 30 minutes for 4-6 hours.
Dry salt all surfaces. Let absorb for 24 hours.
Pierce wheel with sanitized skewers to create air channels for blue development.
Age at 55°F and 95% humidity for 2-3 months, turning weekly.
Once blue veins are well developed, cold smoke at 60-70°F for 2-3 hours.
Age 2-4 more weeks after smoking for flavors to meld.

recipes.temperature: 86°F for make; 60-70°F for smoking; 55°F for aging
notes: Smoke only after blue is well developed
Light smoking preserves blue cheese character
Pairs excellently with bacon and steak

recipes.title: Smoked Brie
recipes.description: Creamy, buttery Brie with light applewood smoke and bloomy white rind, an elegant appetizer cheese.

instructions.text: Combine milk and cream. Heat to 72°F. Add all cultures. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set at 72°F for 12-18 hours.
Gently ladle curds into Brie molds without breaking. Let drain naturally.
Turn molds every 2-3 hours for the first day.
Once firm, remove from molds and salt all surfaces.
Age at 55°F and 95% humidity for 10-14 days until white mold covers surface.
Cold smoke very lightly at 50-60°F for 1-2 hours maximum.
Wrap in cheese paper and continue aging at 45°F for 2-4 more weeks.
Serve when center is soft and oozy.

recipes.temperature: 72°F for make; 50-60°F for smoking; 45-55°F for aging
notes: Very light smoking only - the delicate Brie flavor should remain dominant
Smoke before full ripening so mold can recover
The rind will brown slightly from smoke but white mold should remain

recipes.title: Smoked Swiss Emmental
recipes.description: Sweet, nutty Emmental with characteristic eyes and subtle beechwood smoke, excellent for fondue and sandwiches.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add thermophilic culture and Propionibacterium. Ripen 10 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 25-30 minutes.
Cut curd into rice-sized pieces (1/8 inch). Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise temperature to 125°F over 1 hour, stirring constantly.
Hold at 125°F for 30 minutes until curds are very firm.
Drain and press at 10 lbs for 30 min, then 30 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine in saturated salt solution for 24-36 hours.
Age at 55°F for 2 months, washing with brine weekly.
Move to 70°F 'warm room' for 3-4 weeks for eye development.
Return to 55°F. After 4+ months aging, cold smoke with beechwood at 70-80°F for 4-6 hours.
Continue aging to 8 months for best flavor.

recipes.temperature: 90-125°F for make; 70-80°F for smoking; 55-70°F for aging
notes: The warm room phase is essential for eye development
Larger wheels develop better flavor
Smoke enhances the sweet, nutty character

recipes.title: Hickory Smoked Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Bold American-style smoked cheddar with intense hickory flavor
recipes.description: Sharp, tangy cheddar with bold, bacon-like hickory smoke flavor, perfect for burgers and mac and cheese.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add culture and ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 102°F over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 102°F for 30 more minutes until curds are firm and squeaky.
Drain whey. Mill curds into finger-sized pieces. Salt and mix.
Press at 10 lbs 15 min, 20 lbs 30 min, 50 lbs overnight.
Air dry at room temperature for 3-5 days until rind forms.
Age at 55°F for minimum 3 months.
Cold smoke with hickory at 70-85°F for 6-8 hours over 2 days.
Rest 2 weeks, then continue aging for 3-12 months total.

recipes.temperature: 86-102°F for make; 70-85°F for smoking; 55°F for aging
notes: Hickory gives the strongest smoke flavor - use sparingly at first
Multiple shorter smoking sessions prevent moisture loss
The smoke flavor intensifies with aging

recipes.title: Smoked Monterey Jack
recipes.source_note: Mild California Jack with mesquite smoking
recipes.description: Mild, creamy Monterey Jack with Southwestern mesquite smoke flavor, perfect for quesadillas and Tex-Mex dishes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 88°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise temperature to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Remove 1/3 of whey and replace with same amount of 100°F water. Stir 15 minutes.
Drain whey and salt curds directly.
Press at 10 lbs for 15 min, then 25 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Air dry for 2-3 days until slight rind forms.
Age at 55°F for minimum 4 weeks.
Cold smoke with mesquite at 70-80°F for 4-6 hours.
Continue aging for 1-3 months total.

recipes.temperature: 88-100°F for make; 70-80°F for smoking; 55°F for aging
notes: Mesquite gives a distinctly Southwestern character
Monterey Jack's mild flavor lets the smoke shine
Excellent melting properties for cooking

recipes.title: Garlic and Herb Cream Cheese (Boursin Style)
recipes.source_note: Homemade version of the famous French garlic and herb cheese
recipes.description: Rich, creamy fresh cheese with garlic, herbs, and cracked black pepper, perfect for spreading on crackers or bread.

instructions.text: Combine milk and cream. Heat to 72°F.
Add mesophilic culture. Stir and let ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently and cover.
Let set at room temperature for 12-24 hours until thick like yogurt.
Line colander with butter muslin. Gently ladle curds into cloth.
Tie corners and hang to drain for 12-24 hours until thick and spreadable.
Transfer drained cheese to bowl. Add salt and mix well.
Add garlic, chives, parsley, thyme, and pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Pack into molds or roll into logs. Refrigerate overnight.
Store refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

notes: Use fresh herbs for best flavor
Can substitute dried herbs at 1/3 the amount
Excellent rolled in additional herbs or crushed peppercorns

recipes.title: Dill Havarti
recipes.source_note: Classic Danish Havarti with fresh dill throughout
recipes.description: Creamy, buttery Havarti studded with fresh dill, perfect for sandwiches and Scandinavian dishes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir for 10 minutes, then let curds settle.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Add 170°F water to raise temperature to 100°F.
Stir at 100°F for 15 minutes until curds are springy.
Drain most whey. Add chopped dill and mix thoroughly with curds.
Press at 8 lbs for 30 min, 15 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours in saturated salt solution.
Air dry for 2-3 days, then wax or vacuum seal.
Age at 55°F for 2-3 months.

notes: Fresh dill is essential - dried dill doesn't work as well
Can also make caraway Havarti using 2 tbsp caraway seeds
The dill flavor intensifies with aging

recipes.title: Sage Derby
recipes.source_note: Historic English cheese with sage leaves creating green marbling
recipes.description: Mild, mellow Derby cheese with distinctive green marbling from sage leaves, a British Christmas tradition.

instructions.text: Blend sage (and spinach if using) with 1 cup of the milk until smooth green liquid.
Strain through fine mesh, pressing to extract all green juice.
Heat remaining milk to 86°F. Add culture and ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 94°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey and divide curds in half. Add sage juice to one half, mixing well.
Layer plain and green curds alternately in mold for marbled effect.
Press at 10 lbs for 15 min, 30 lbs for 4-6 hours.
Salt all surfaces. Air dry for 3-5 days.
Age at 55°F for 1-3 months, turning weekly.

notes: Traditional Sage Derby uses only sage juice for green color
Spinach boosts the green color without affecting flavor
The marbled pattern makes beautiful slices
Traditional Christmas cheese in England

recipes.title: Cumin Gouda (Komijnekaas)
recipes.source_note: Classic Dutch Gouda with cumin seeds (Leidse kaas style)
recipes.description: Creamy Dutch Gouda studded with aromatic cumin seeds, a traditional Leiden specialty.

instructions.text: Toast cumin seeds in dry pan until fragrant. Set aside to cool.
Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Replace with 175°F water. This washes the curds.
Stir at 100°F for 20 minutes until curds are firm.
Drain whey. Add toasted cumin seeds and mix thoroughly.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours in saturated salt solution.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-6 months.

notes: Toasting the cumin brings out more flavor
Traditional Leiden cheese also adds caraway
Excellent with dark bread and mustard

recipes.title: Lavender Honey Chèvre
recipes.source_note: Aromatic fresh goat cheese with lavender and honey
recipes.description: Delicate fresh goat cheese infused with culinary lavender and drizzled with local honey, a Provençal delicacy.

instructions.text: Heat goat milk to 72°F. Add mesophilic culture. Stir and let ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently for 30 seconds.
Cover and let set at room temperature for 18-24 hours until thick.
Gently ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined molds.
Let drain 24-48 hours until desired consistency.
Unmold cheese and add salt, mixing gently.
Crush lavender buds slightly and fold into cheese.
Form into logs or rounds. Drizzle with honey before serving.
Store refrigerated for up to 10 days.

notes: Use only culinary-grade lavender (pesticide-free)
Herbes de Provence can substitute for lavender
Pairs beautifully with fresh fruit and crusty bread

recipes.title: Nettle Gouda (Brandnetelkaas)
recipes.source_note: Dutch Gouda with stinging nettles giving green flecks and earthy flavor
recipes.description: Creamy Gouda with distinctive green flecks from stinging nettles, offering a subtle earthy, spinach-like flavor.

instructions.text: Wearing gloves, blanch nettles in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain, squeeze dry, and chop fine.
Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Remove 1/3 whey. Replace with 175°F water. Continue stirring 20 minutes.
Drain whey. Add prepared nettles to curds and mix thoroughly.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-4 months.

notes: Always blanch nettles first to remove sting
Spring nettles have the best flavor
Can substitute spinach if nettles unavailable

recipes.title: Fenugreek Gouda
recipes.source_note: Dutch Gouda with fenugreek seeds for maple-like sweetness
recipes.description: Creamy Gouda studded with fenugreek seeds that add a distinctive maple and curry-like aroma.

instructions.text: Lightly crush fenugreek seeds to release flavor.
Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Remove 1/3 whey. Replace with 175°F water. Continue stirring 20 minutes.
Drain whey. Add fenugreek seeds and mix thoroughly.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-4 months.

notes: Fenugreek has a distinctive maple-curry aroma
Popular in Dutch and German cheesemaking
Pairs well with Indian and Middle Eastern cuisines

recipes.title: Rosemary Manchego
recipes.source_note: Traditional Manchego pressed with fresh rosemary
recipes.description: Firm, buttery Manchego with aromatic rosemary pressed into the rind and throughout, perfect with Spanish wines.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F. Add thermophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 104°F over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 104°F for 30 more minutes until curds are firm.
Drain whey. Add minced rosemary to curds and mix.
Line mold with rosemary sprigs. Add curds and press.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 25 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Dry salt by rubbing salt on all surfaces for 24 hours.
Rub with olive oil. Age at 55°F for 2-6 months.

notes: The rosemary sprigs create beautiful imprint on rind
Traditional Manchego uses esparto grass molds
Pairs wonderfully with membrillo (quince paste)

recipes.title: Black Pepper Pecorino (Pecorino al Pepe)
recipes.source_note: Tuscan/Roman sheep's milk cheese with cracked black pepper
recipes.description: Sharp, tangy sheep's milk cheese with generous cracked black pepper throughout and coating the rind.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 90°F. Add thermophilic culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 116°F over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 116°F for 15 minutes until curds are quite firm.
Drain whey. Add half the cracked pepper to curds and mix.
Press at 15 lbs for 1 hour, flip, then 30 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Dry salt all surfaces. Age 1-2 days.
Coat exterior with remaining cracked pepper, pressing into rind.
Age at 55°F for 2-8 months, turning weekly.

notes: Use high-quality peppercorns for best flavor
The pepper flavor intensifies with aging
Essential for authentic cacio e pepe pasta

recipes.title: Époisses de Bourgogne (Burgundy Wine-Washed)
recipes.source_note: Famous French washed-rind cheese washed with Marc de Bourgogne
recipes.description: Pungent, creamy washed-rind cheese with sticky orange rind from washings with Marc de Bourgogne brandy.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 90 minutes.
Gently ladle curds into Époisses molds without breaking.
Let drain naturally 24 hours, turning every 6 hours.
Salt all surfaces. Let cure 24 hours.
Move to aging cave at 55°F and 95% humidity.
Mix Marc with equal parts light brine. Wash cheese every 2-3 days.
Continue washing and aging for 6-8 weeks until rind is sticky orange and interior is soft.
Wrap in paper and store refrigerated. Serve at room temperature.

notes: Marc de Bourgogne is grape pomace brandy - substitute cognac if unavailable
The smell is strong but the flavor is complex and mild
One of France's most famous (and pungent) cheeses
Banned on public transport in France due to its aroma!

recipes.title: Port Wine Washed Cheese
recipes.source_note: Semi-soft cheese with ruby Port wine wash creating deep purple rind
recipes.description: Creamy semi-soft cheese with beautiful purple-stained rind from Port wine washings and subtle grape sweetness.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 98°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 4 hours.
Salt all surfaces. Age at 55°F and 90% humidity.
After 1 week, begin washing with Port wine every 2-3 days.
Continue washing for 4-8 weeks until rind is deep purple and cheese is semi-soft.

notes: Ruby Port gives the deepest color; tawny works too
The alcohol evaporates but the grape flavor remains
Beautiful centerpiece for cheese boards

recipes.title: Beer-Washed Cheese (Bierkäse)
recipes.source_note: Semi-soft cheese washed with Belgian-style ale
recipes.description: Pungent, meaty washed-rind cheese with complex flavors from beer washings, perfect with crusty bread.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 4 hours.
Brine for 4-6 hours in saturated salt solution.
Age at 55°F and 95% humidity.
After 1 week, begin washing with beer every 2-3 days.
Continue washing for 6-10 weeks until rind is sticky and orange-brown.

notes: Belgian abbey ales and German doppelbock work excellently
The beer contributes yeast and malt flavors
Pairs perfectly with the same beer used for washing

recipes.title: Irish Whiskey Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Sharp Irish cheddar soaked in Irish whiskey
recipes.description: Sharp, crumbly Irish cheddar infused with Irish whiskey, offering warm, oaky notes with vanilla undertones.

instructions.text: Make cheddar using standard method: heat milk to 86°F, add culture, ripen 45 min.
Add calcium chloride and rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut curd 1/4-inch. Heat slowly to 102°F over 30 minutes.
Hold at 102°F for 30 minutes until curds are firm and squeaky.
Drain whey. Mill curds and salt. Press overnight at 50 lbs.
Age cheddar at 55°F for minimum 3 months.
Cut aged wheel into quarters. Soak in Irish whiskey for 24-48 hours.
Remove, pat dry, and wrap. Age 1-2 more weeks for flavors to meld.
Alternatively: Brush wheel with whiskey weekly during final month of aging.

notes: Jameson or Powers work well for this
The whiskey flavor mellows with additional aging
A wonderful after-dinner cheese with Irish coffee

recipes.title: Grappa-Washed Italian Cheese (Ubriaco)
recipes.source_note: Aged Italian cheese soaked in grape marc and grappa
recipes.description: Firm, tangy cheese aged in grape skins and washed with grappa, with distinctive purple color and winey flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add thermophilic culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride and rennet. Set 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Slowly raise to 110°F over 30 minutes.
Drain whey. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 40 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine for 12-24 hours.
Age at 55°F for minimum 2 months.
Mix grape marc with grappa. Bury cheese in the marc mixture.
Store covered at 55°F for 2-4 months, turning occasionally.
Remove from marc. The rind will be deep purple. Age 2 more weeks before serving.

notes: Ubriaco means 'drunken' in Italian
Red wine grape marc gives the most color
The cheese absorbs wine and fruit flavors from the marc
Traditional in the Veneto region during grape harvest

recipes.title: Calvados-Washed Camembert
recipes.source_note: Classic Normandy Camembert washed with apple brandy
recipes.description: Rich, creamy Camembert with bloomy rind brushed with Calvados apple brandy, adding fruity complexity.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add mesophilic culture, P. candidum, and G. candidum. Ripen 90 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 90 minutes.
Carefully ladle curds into Camembert molds. Let drain overnight.
Turn molds several times during draining.
Salt all surfaces. Let drain 1 more day.
Move to aging cave at 55°F and 95% humidity.
After white mold appears (7-10 days), brush with Calvados every 3-4 days.
Continue aging and occasional Calvados washing for 4-6 weeks.
Cheese is ready when center feels soft when pressed.

notes: Calvados is essential for authentic Norman flavor
American apple brandy or applejack can substitute
The apple notes pair beautifully with the mushroomy Camembert

recipes.title: Cider-Washed Farmhouse Cheese
recipes.source_note: Traditional farmhouse cheese washed with hard cider
recipes.description: Semi-soft farmhouse cheese with sticky orange rind from cider washings, offering tangy apple notes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 88°F. Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 4 hours.
Brine for 6-8 hours.
Age at 55°F and 95% humidity.
After 1 week, begin washing with hard cider every 2-3 days.
